description: Visa is a payment technology company headquartered in San Francisco and operating in the United States and internationally. It runs VisaNet, one of the world’s largest electronic payments processing networks, and offers credit, debit, and prepaid card products, as well as tap- and click-to-pay services. Launched by Bank of America in 1958 as BankAmericard, the Visa card was the first general-purpose credit card to offer revolving credit. The Visa brand was established in 1976, and Visa became a publicly traded, independent company in 2008 after a historic IPO.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
Visa says it adheres to its Employee Value Proposition of “Powering payments, empowering people.” The digital payments giant’s new 32,000-square-foot location in Atlanta, welcoming 500 employees, was designed and constructed in collaboration with suppliers of diverse backgrounds. To help staff build professional development skills, the company provides access to Visa University for all employees, with senior staff serving as faculty. Among the courses offered are “The Leader as Coach,” which includes one-on-one sessions delivered through the BetterUp platform.
 

Through its Visa Foundation, the company matched employee donations of up to $10,000 and double-matched up to $1,000 on Giving Tuesday in 2023, in which 4,890 staff participated. Combined with the match program, employees donated $7.1 million to over 4,200 organizations.
 

In an effort to address climate change, Visa offers 75 electric-vehicle chargers and free charging for employees, bicycle parking, local and vegan food options, and a shuttle service that minimizes individual car emissions at its Foster City, Calif., headquarters.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
The digital payments operator recently opened a new office in Atlanta, as part of its efforts to diversify its workforce.

  • The Visa Health Center is open to all U.S.-based employees enrolled in an employee health plan. The center offers primary care, mental health support, and physical therapy.

  • In 2022, Visa hosted its first Global Inclusion and Diversity Summit, where the company introduced its strategy to increase diversity among staff and suppliers.

  • This past year, Visa welcomed 72 more students into its Black Scholars and Jobs Program, reaching a total of 126 student participants for the 2021 and 2022 program years. Participants from the first cohort were offered internships at Visa for the summer of 2023. The inaugural class of scholars attended the first Visa Black Scholars Summit, which included workshops and networking opportunities for participants.

  • The company holds a pay equity analysis annually to ensure that it’s paying employees equally regardless of gender or race. This information is public and accessible to employees.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: The credit card and payments powerhouse, which commands a 50% market share of total card payments worldwide, saw its business slump in 2020 as the pandemic caused a slowdown in economic activity. Its sales slid 5% to $21.9 billion and profits dropped by 10%, but it still moved up four spots to No. 133 on relative strength in a tough year.
